I've read the complete implementation. It's a minimal Express + vanilla-JS bookmark manager: a JSON file store with list/search/tag-filter/create/edit/delete endpoints and a single-page UI. I'll judge each requirement from the code only.

Key observations from the code:
- **Data model** (`server.js`): bookmark = `{id, url, title, description, tags, createdAt, updatedAt}`. No `note`, `unread`, `archived`, `favicon`, `preview`, `snapshot` fields.
- **No metadata fetching** on save (title defaults to url).
- **POST** always `items.push` — no duplicate-url convergence.
- **Search** filters title/url/description/tags with `includes(q.toLowerCase())` — case-insensitive, but no `#tag` syntax, no boolean/parentheses, no phrase matching, no note.
- **Tags**: assignable, filterable by click; input is plain text (no autocomplete/datalist).
- **Sort**: fixed `createdAt` desc, no key selection.
- **No** unread, archive, bulk actions, snapshots, bundles, import/export, or settings anywhere.
